extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, and attorneys handling practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Reciprocal disciplinary process under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 by which the USPTO Director may impose discipline identical to a state court's suspension; includes notice, opportunity to respond, standards for decision, publication, and notice to other authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: A Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 may be filed requesting that the Director impose reciprocal discipline upon a respondent identical to the discipline imposed by a state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must be mailed to the respondent (example shows certified mail), and the respondent is given an opportunity to file, within forty days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and effect of no response
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is provided forty days to file a response to the Notice and Order opposing reciprocal discipline under the enumerated grounds in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent does not file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and conclude that reciprocal suspension identical to the state discipline is appropriate (as here, suspension for three years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical standard invoked (37 C.F.R. § 10.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension was ordered for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may base reciprocal discipline on the cited USPTO ethical provisions in conjunction with state court findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: State court findings as basis for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's reciprocal discipline can be predicated upon the state supreme court's findings and order (here, the Supreme Court of New Hampshire's suspension dated September 6, 2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The state court's factual findings (including reasons for imposing or enforcing a stayed suspension) are used to justify imposing identical discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific lawyer conduct violations relied upon (state RPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state suspension was predicated upon violations of New Hampshire Rules of Professional Conduct: Rule 1.3; Rule 1.4(a)-(c); Rule 8.1(a); Rule 8.4(c); and Rule 8.4(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document explains the conduct underlying those rules: failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (Rule 1.3); failing to forward important documents and explain legal/practical aspects to clients (Rule 1.4(a)-(c)); making a false statement of material fact to the Attorney Discipline Office (Rule 8.1(a)); making false statements to clients about mishandling of cases (Rule 8.4(c)); and generally violating the Rules of Professional Conduct (Rule 8.4(a)). These state-rule violations form the factual predicate for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration of suspension before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The order suspends the respondent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO for a specified period (three years in this case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the Director is identical in scope/duration to the state-imposed discipline unless successfully opposed under the procedural grounds in § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 / Official Gazette notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, identifying the respondent and registration number, and stating the reasons for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example notice text includes: identification of respondent and registration number; statement that respondent was suspended and for what period; citation to the violated rules and state court order date; statutory/regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59); and a reference to the OED Reading Room for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other jurisdictions and relevant courts are informed of the USPTO action; the order explicitly directs the OED Director to provide such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reciprocal discipline proceeding should cite and rely upon these statutory/regulatory provisions as the basis for authority to impose discipline on practitioners before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service method and record of service for Notices/Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices and Orders in reciprocal discipline proceedings should be mailed (example shows certified mail) and a delivery date/receipt recorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example shows certified mail with receipt number and a recorded delivery date (Notice mailed Dec. 15, 2011; delivered Dec. 19, 2011), which supports that the respondent received the Notice and was thereby afforded the procedural response period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of disciplinary decisions via OED Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (link provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers of notices and parties seeking prior decisions may consult the OED Reading Room (FOIA link in example) for related disciplinary decisions and precedents.
